Add a licence-name gate with an allowlist (#287)

Add tools/check-licence-names.py, its allowlist
tools/licence-names-allowlist.tsv and its tests
tools/test-check-licence-names.py. The gate lists the tracked files
with git ls-files, reads each from the work tree, splits it at line
feeds only and finds every line that holds 1 of its 3 search terms in
any ASCII letter case; its docstring names the terms. The gate fails
on a matching line that no row of its path claims (unclaimed); on a
matching line that holds the markers of 2 or more rows of its path
(ambiguous), which none of those rows claims, so a broad marker cannot
quietly take lines of another kind; on a row whose claimed lines
differ in number from its count (stale), fewer or more, which includes
a row whose lines are gone, though a row of a path that cannot be read
is not reported stale, since its lines are unknown; and on a malformed
row, which claims nothing: a row with a number of fields other than 4,
a carriage return, a count that is not canonical ASCII decimal, an
owner other than unit-2, unit-3 or keep, an empty marker, a path that
is not tracked, a path of a named exception, or the path and marker of
an earlier row that has 4 fields and no carriage return, whether or
not that earlier row is well formed. It compares a count as text, so a
wrong count of any length gives a named problem. The gate fails
closed, exiting 1 and naming the cause, and turns no error into an
empty or clean result: when git ls-files cannot run, fails or lists
nothing; when it gives an entry that cannot be read (one with no tab,
or without exactly 3 fields before its tab); when an entry is unmerged
(a stage other than 0); when a tracked path has a mode other than
100644 or 100755, such as a symbolic link (120000) or a submodule
(160000); when a tracked path is not a regular file in the work tree
(which includes a path that is absolute, a path with a part that is
empty, a single dot or 2 dots, and a path with a parent at any depth
that is a symbolic link or anything else but a folder) or cannot be
opened or read; and when the allowlist cannot be read or is not UTF-8.
When git ls-files lists entries and the gate can read none of them, it
names each entry and no other cause. It opens each tracked path 1 part
at a time from the repository root, never through a symbolic link, so
it reads no tracked path from outside the work tree. It runs git with
a fixed argument list and no shell and treats file content as data. It
makes git's message and an error's text 1 line and cuts them to 300
characters; then, in each field that it shows, it writes a backslash
and each character outside printable ASCII once as a backslash escape.
Its own 3 files are its named exceptions; each must be tracked and
must hold a matching line. The allowlist has 1 row per kind of line in
a file: path, count, owner and marker. The gate refuses an owner other
than unit-2, unit-3 or keep; whether a row's owner is the right one is
reviewed, and the gate does not check it.

The gate's docstring states what it does not cover. Not covered:
another spelling of a licence, such as one in words without the 3
terms, a term split over 2 lines or a lookalike character outside
ASCII; untracked and ignored files; the index copy of a file whose
work-tree copy differs (in CI they are equal); a folder of the work
tree that is a mount point and a file that is a hard link, each read
where it stands; whether a line is a true statement of a licence;
whether the owner of a row is right, which is reviewed prose; and the
named exceptions' own lines. A row counts lines per file, so fixing 1
line and adding another of the same kind in the same file passes.

The tests build throwaway git repositories and run the gate with no
setting of git taken from the caller's environment or configuration.
Each refusal case that runs the gate first runs it on the unchanged
repository, which must pass, then makes the change that it tests, to
the repository or to the gate's PATH, in 1 or more steps, such as
tracking a file and then deleting it from the work tree. It then
requires exit 1, exactly 1 summary line on standard output (for
--list, only path:count lines and then a total line), and problem
lines that match, 1 for 1, the cause and any consequence that the case
names with its reason, with none left over. Each subtest makes its
change to the unchanged repository. No run of the gate may write a
character outside printable ASCII. 5 cases call the gate's file reader
in a separate python3 -I process that loads the gate by file path: 1
reads a regular file as a control, and 4 replace os.lstat or os.fdopen
in that process alone to reach an open descriptor that is not a
regular file, a symbolic link that appears after the lstat check, and
a read error, once with the system's text and once with a text of
whitespace, characters outside printable ASCII, a backslash and more
than 300 characters. 6 cases give the gate a stand-in git, a Python
script alone on its PATH: 1 exits 3 with a message like that text; 1
lists the repository's 4 files and paths that are not plain relative,
1 of them leading out of the work tree, to the gate and to --list; and
4 list 3 entries that cannot be read, 1 with no tab, 1 with 2 fields
before its tab and 1 with 4, to the gate and to --list, 2 beside the
repository's 4 files and 2 alone.

The Agent Plugins manifest workflow runs the tests and the gate as 2
new steps, and tools/run_all_checks.sh runs them as 2 new run lines.
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of that script.
.github/squash/287.txt holds this message.

Checks a reviewer can rerun from the repository root, with their
expected outcomes:

    python3 -I tools/check-licence-names.py

exits 0, and at the head of this change its last line is
"check-licence-names: checked: 59 lines in 35 files; 0 problem(s)".

    python3 -I tools/check-licence-names.py --list

exits 0 and prints 1 line of path and count per file, then the line
"total: 59 lines in 35 files".

    python3 -I tools/test-check-licence-names.py
    python3 -I tools/test-run-all-checks.py

each exit 0.
